subject.title: [Feature]: SSH-verified auto-approval for node device pairing

question: Should OpenClaw core add a distinct, disabled-by-default SSH-verified automatic device-pairing policy after the silent node-surface regression is repaired?
rationale: Source inspection proves the missing propagation, but code cannot decide whether the gateway should initiate SSH during authentication, what destinations it may contact, or whether cross-host automatic trust should become default behavior.

options.title: Split repair and opt-in policy
options.body: Fix silent provenance propagation first, then review a separate disabled-by-default SSH verifier with a distinct approval kind.

options.title: Enable SSH verification by default
options.body: Attempt strict SSH identity verification automatically for eligible private and CGNAT first-time node peers.

options.title: Repair existing behavior only
options.body: Restore the documented macOS silent path and retain manual or explicit CIDR pairing as the available policies.

recommendation.title: Split repair and opt-in policy
recommendation.body: Fix silent provenance propagation first, then review a separate disabled-by-default SSH verifier with a distinct approval kind.

likelyOwner.reason: This person introduced the current reconciliation path, recently refactored pairing state, and authored the proposed security design.
